title: Married filing separately and lived apart all year, benefits $4,000, wages $8,000: none taxable

source.where: Publication 915 (2026), Worksheet 1 line 9: $25,000 if married filing separately and you lived apart from your spouse for all of 2026

note: Line 6 is 8,000 + half the benefits 2,000 = 10,000, under the 25,000 base: nothing taxable. (Example 4's person, who lived with the spouse, has 3,400 taxable.)

title: Married filing separately, lived together, benefits $10,000, wages $40,000: 85% of the benefits, $8,500

source.where: Publication 915 (2026), Worksheet 1 lines 17 to 19: 85% of line 8, never more than 85% of the benefits

title: Single, benefits $10,000, wages $30,000, a $2,000 IRA deduction comes off first: $4,000 taxable

source.where: Publication 915 (2026), Worksheet 1 line 7: Schedule 1 lines 11 to 20, 23 and 25 (an IRA deduction), subtracted from line 6

note: Line 2 is 5,000; line 6 is 30,000 + 5,000 = 35,000; line 7 (the IRA deduction) 2,000; line 8 is 33,000. Line 10 is 33,000 - 25,000 = 8,000; line 11 is 9,000; line 12 is 0; line 13 is 8,000; line 14 is 4,000; line 15 is the smaller of 5,000 and 4,000 = 4,000; line 16 is 0; line 17 is 4,000; line 18 is 85% of 10,000 = 8,500; line 19 is 4,000. (Without the adjustment line 8 is 35,000 and 5,350 would be taxable.)

title: Single, age 64 at year end, born January 1, 1962, wages $30,000: the extra standard deduction counts (65 the day before)

source.where: Publication 501 (2025), Higher Standard Deduction for Age: you are considered 65 on the day before your 65th birthday (born before January 2, 1961 for 2025, so before January 2, 1962 for 2026)

note: 16,100 + 2,050 = 18,150: born 1962-01-01, the 65th birthday is 2027-01-01 and the day before is 2026-12-31.

title: Single, age 64 at year end, born January 2, 1962, wages $30,000: no extra standard deduction

source.where: Publication 501 (2025), Higher Standard Deduction for Age: you are considered 65 on the day before your 65th birthday

note: The 65th birthday is 2027-01-02, the day before is 2027-01-01: 65 in 2027, not 2026. Standard 16,100.
